name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Scenic hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with pine forests, colonial architecture, lakes, waterfalls, and vibrant Khasi culture. Main gateway for the region.
facts: Capital of Meghalaya and HQ of East Khasi Hills
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong on Shillong Peak
Nearest airport Umroi; major access via Guwahati

name: Jowai
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills and cultural hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) community. Located on a plateau at about 1,365 m elevation, surrounded by the Myntdu River. Gateway for exploring waterfalls, monoliths, lakes and the Behdeinkhlam festival.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district
Home of the annual Behdeinkhlam festival

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning multi-tiered waterfall with turquoise blue plunge pools in the Amlarem area of West Jaintia Hills. Surrounded by lush forests and limestone formations; involves a short trek. One of Meghalaya’s most photogenic falls.
facts: Located in Amlarem, ~90 km from Shillong

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megalithic monoliths (menhirs and dolmens) in Meghalaya, north of Nartiang market. Erected by Jaintia clans between the 16th and 19th centuries to commemorate victories and ancestors. Includes the tallest menhir in the region.
facts: Largest monolith cluster in Khasi-Jaintia Hills
Tallest menhir erected by U Mar Phalyngki

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient 500-600 year old Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti Devi), one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Located in Nartiang village; historically associated with the Jaintia kings and once used for ritual sacrifices.
facts: Near Jowai in West Jaintia Hills

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Man-made historical lake on NH-6 near Mukhla village, about 8 km from Jowai. Created according to legend by Sajar Nangli and followers using bow ends; popular picnic and boating spot with scenic surroundings.
facts: Also known as Pung Sajar Nangli
Man-made by legend of Sajar Nangli

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Famous crystal-clear Umngot River at the India-Bangladesh border town of Dawki. Boating under the 1932 British suspension bridge offers floating boat effect in dry season; one of India’s cleanest rivers.
facts: Umngot River considered one of India’s cleanest

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Quiet riverside village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River. Preferred for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping and clearer water away from border traffic; emerging eco-tourism spot in West Jaintia Hills.
facts: Ideal for river camping and adventure
Clearer water than Dawki in season
Accessible by local taxi from Dawki

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, cascading over rocks amid lush greenery. Often compared to Elephant Falls; short walk from the main road via an arch bridge.
facts: Less crowded alternative to major falls

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Hidden two-tiered waterfall in the forests near Shkentalang village, West Jaintia Hills. Features turquoise pools and requires a moderate forest trek; one of Meghalaya’s lesser-known gems.
facts: About 22 km from Jowai near Shkentalang

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai with sacred grove, gardens and panoramic views of the Pynthor Wah valley and Myntdu River. Popular for picnics and short nature walks.
facts: Official tourist place of the district

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Scenic valley and historical ground irrigated by the Myntdu River near Jowai, also called Madan Madiah. Site of U Kiang Nangbah memorial commemorating the Jaintia freedom fighter; offers panoramic views.
facts: Home to U Kiang Nangbah memorial
